claims.text: Successful formation of noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles is governed by kinetic control of nanoparticle formation.
Metal-precursor reduction kinetics dictate nanoparticle morphology and composition.
The entropy of mixing in the nanocrystals dictates nanoparticle morphology and composition.
Controlling precursor reduction while optimizing entropy of mixing will promote successful nanoparticle formation.
Entropy of mixing in the nanocrystals is the structural mediator.
Metal-precursor reduction kinetics influence nanoparticle nucleation and growth.
The intervention will increase surface-atom exposure by 30% relative to uncontrolled-morphology nanoparticles.
The intervention will decrease decomposition temperature by 25% relative to uncontrolled-morphology nanoparticles.
The proposed scope includes nanoparticles containing more than five interacting elements.
The proposed scope includes nanoparticles characterized by high decomposition temperatures and uncontrolled morphology.
A controlled comparison varying reduction kinetics and entropy of mixing can test the hypothesis.
The hypothesis is falsified if the predicted outcome is absent, surface-atom exposure is less than 20% above baseline, and decomposition temperature is more than 15% above baseline.
